experiment_kind: independent prototype control-window review, not production route acceptance
inferred_requirements: Require a physically contiguous complete logical-instruction interval ending at CALL, not a filtered set of arbitrary LOADs.
Reject every internal ordinary jump target and exception-handler target; allow first-offset entry.
Retain every required LOAD suboperand and CALL INSTRUCTION on every execution; static membership alone is not an execution witness.
Retain all CALL-family attempt barriers and persistent normal-continuation/handler expiry callbacks even when initially no pending attempt.
Rebuild windows offline from exactly matched source-compiled CodeType, with capture rule selected per PID.
Reject suspended caller code under the new narrow rule; do not join generator resumes.
Keep all original interference, delivery continuity, namespace, source, environment and effect conditions.

official_docs.version_caveat: Online documentation currently 3.14.8; experiments used local CPython 3.14.7.

unsupported_or_not_proved: The unbound-local exception case yielded zero narrow windows; this is an explicit grammar boundary, not successful exception routing.
Generator control windows were measured only to audit event isolation; this is not permission to route suspended callers.
No dynamic branch-to-core predecessor selection or whole-program graph closure is proved.
A monitoring callback can be replaced or disabled and restored without a durable mask difference; static CFG guards cannot prove delivery continuity.
No LeWM performance claim follows from prototype callback counts.
